Constraint satisfaction: final author review

Date: 18 October 2026. The complete new English chapter remains a student-unapproved author-review draft.

Instruction and question-by-question reasoning

Twenty-five teaching sections develop finite relations, modeling, assignment counts, backtracking proofs, deterministic heuristics, directed supports, queue invariants, exact rollback, tree construction/counting, cutsets, global constraints, stronger consistency, conflicts, repair and weighted bounds. Fifty original/attributed problems include numeric calculations, proof obligations, asymptotic assumptions and counterexamples. Four additional authentic MS placements preserve exact original choices and explain every decisive inference. The cycle-coloring solution now derives its closed form through an explicit induction step rather than asserting it. Sixty-four final decisions use complete sentences and identify the assumption behind each rule.

Six actual written university scopes were synthesized. Stanford, Berkeley, CMU and MIT are complementary primaries; Cornell and Harvard provide substantive additional checks. Seven candidate offerings were evaluated. Exact reading ranges, local acquisition failures, omitted protected material, source errors and the bounded prompt inventory are recorded in the source audit and ledger. This is not a worldwide exhaustive-course claim.

The original numeric and map questions were checked against source-page images and pinned PDF fingerprints. No official answer key was verified, and no doctoral CSP item was verified in the bounded archive pass. The 1402 edge/arc wording and 1405 omitted tree premise are preserved as explicit source qualifications. The map's three-color interactive example is labeled as a teaching assumption.

Mathematics and executable reference

The actual Python listing was extracted from the rendered HTML and executed, with byte-level source agreement. It was compared against independent direct enumeration on all 4096 three-variable Boolean binary-table systems, including empty relations. Plain search, forward checking, MAC, complete enumeration and first-solution mode agreed with the independent solution sets. Propagation preserved all genuine solutions and every successful closure had the required support witnesses.

The reference now uses a separate queued set for expected constant-time queue-membership checks and avoids making before-state snapshots when recording is disabled. Its teaching-output memory is excluded from the lean solver-state bound. Reversed duplicate constraints are conjoined; initially empty isolated domains and the empty variable set are handled correctly. General mathematical correctness relies on the stated invariants/proofs in addition to finite tests.

The mathematics report records 39399 assertions, including 319 exact serialized support-witness checks, all 720 initial queue permutations of the authentic numeric problem, queen attacks, cycle counts and notation structure. Queue order changed that problem's revision count from 6 through 8 while preserving the successful closure. All 749 native MathML expressions passed delimiter, closing-script-base and arity inspection. Explicit raw mathematical expressions in prose were converted to native notation rather than left as unformatted subscripts or Unicode exponent strings.

Diagrams, interaction and presentation

Twenty-six exact finite domain/queue cases occur in 28 player placements. All 335 displayed placement/checkpoints passed actual Edge text-padding, connector-endpoint and support-table checks. Five additional interactive board/matching placements use distinct concept mechanisms: actual queen coordinates/attacking pairs and all-different bipartite matchings. A higher-arity factor diagram, original map reconstruction and actual-input tables explain structure, counting, weighted factors, beams and conflict merging.

The editable binary-table laboratory independently implements support filtering in JavaScript. All 4096 corresponding finite inputs matched the exact Python closure/failure result; endpoint and reversed-conjunction cases passed. Ten invalid-input checks rejected malformed data. Twenty-eight player controls and three real playbacks passed; three queen placements reproduced conflict scores 4,2,2,2 and both valid boards, and two Hall placements traversed all declared support claims.

Newsreader headings, Source Sans 3 prose, STIX Two Math notation and JetBrains Mono code loaded. The document stayed within 390,768 and 1360 pixel viewports. A genuine long-example-selector overflow was repaired with constrained responsive sizing. Compact graph canvases scroll locally on narrow screens. No links or solution summaries are underlined. Print exposes all 54 solutions and 60 initial/failure/final graph snapshots, then restores the reader's previous open/closed answer state. Five representative rendered views were visually inspected, including formula and map views. This checks actual Edge behavior and print DOM/CSS, not every browser or every paginated PDF break.

Status and limits

Source, mathematical, question, model and browser gates are complete for this edition. Finite verification is not literal universal correctness or an unseen-examination score guarantee. The chapter adds one technical draft; it does not count as another revision of the original sixty-chapter baseline. Publication provenance and GitHub synchronization are recorded separately after their actual success.
